# Independent audit: attained sampled convex residual thresholds


`candidate 3869d933360d8c9c`.


its already audited conditional form. This note adds an attained finite
optimization and an actual strict comparison with affine hinges; it
does not prove a universal bound on the optimized residual.

## Attainment and exact interpolation

There are finitely many positive intrinsic fibers and finitely many
subsets of the given cap family of size at most t. Thus each sampled
residual root e_p is finite and attained, including e_p=0 and the empty
cap subset. The variables h_p,g_p satisfy finitely many non-strict
linear inequalities. A constant h at least max e_p is feasible with
g_p=0. Eliminating all slope coordinates gives a closed polyhedron
of feasible h values. On the nonnegative orthant, every sublevel
sum h_p^q<=R is bounded and closed for each integer q>=1. A minimizing
h therefore exists, and membership in the projected set supplies
actual finite slopes. This does not assume bounded slopes along an
arbitrary minimizing sequence.

For the polyhedral extension

    ell(z)=max(0,max_p [h_p+g_p.(z-p)]),

the own plane gives ell(p)>=h_p. Each other plane is bounded above
by h_p by the matching interpolation constraint, and 0<=h_p.
Therefore ell(p)=h_p exactly. The extension is a finite nonnegative
convex function on conv(P), so the approximate-cover theorem applies.

Conversely, sampled values h_p=ell(p) of ANY finite convex function
on conv(P) satisfy the interpolation constraints with some finite
g_p, even if ell has no subgradient at a boundary base. For fixed p,
the finite alternative to feasibility is a nonnegative lambda with

    sum_r lambda_r(r-p)=0,
    sum_r lambda_r(h_r-h_p)<0.

Its positive total normalizes to a convex representation of p,
contradicting Jensen's inequality at the finitely many sample points.
This verifies the boundary-point claim without silently imposing
lower semicontinuity or an ambient-domain extension on ell.

The source's proof of the finite alternative is valid: range(A) is
generated conically by signed basis vectors, so range(A)+R_+^m is
finitely generated. Reducing any nonnegative representation to an
independent subset and passing to a fixed subset proves this cone
closed. Separation yields A^T lambda=0, lambda>=0, and the stated
strict inequality. All signs agree with the system A g<=b.

Consequently R_conv is the exact attained minimum over all admissible
finite convex thresholds, not only over a smaller interpolating class.
Every affine hinge is in that class, so comparison with its attained
minimum has the claimed direction.

## Cap budget and intrinsic scope

The original approximate-cover theorem selects at most kt original
caps, retaining the sampled threshold at every positive fiber.
Finite subadditivity therefore gives

    kt B >= M-R_conv.

If R_conv<=(1-tg)M and 0<=tg<=1, division by the positive integer t
gives B>=gM/k. The count k remains the occupied parity count; it is
not the number of convex pieces in the new extension. Intrinsic q
is positive here. The separate counting argument is not replaced
by a zero-th-root convention. Actual strict residual complements,
oblique caps, and closed vertical caps are inherited exactly from
the intrinsic theorem; no approximate change of their traces occurs.

## Exact actual hinge gap

For C=[0,1]^2 x [0,1]^q, q>=1, the four actual integer fibers have
unit q-volume. The two proposed closed vertical caps capture exactly
the off-diagonal fibers, separately. Thus for t=1 or t=2 the residual
roots are 1 at (0,0),(1,1) and 0 at (1,0),(0,1). The convex function
|z_1+z_2-1| matches these four values. Hence the convex optimum is
exactly 2: its value is attained, and the two forced entries already
contribute 2 to every objective.

For an admissible affine hinge, its untruncated affine values a,c
at the diagonal bases satisfy a,c>=1. The other values b,d satisfy
b+d=a+c>=2, by the affine parallelogram identity. Therefore

    a^q+c^q>=2,
    (b_+)^q+(d_+)^q>=2*((b_++d_+)/2)^q>=2.

These inequalities use only q>=1 and include q=1. The constant affine
function 1 attains objective 4, establishing the exact strict gap
R_conv=2<4=R_hinge. All fibers and cap arrays are actual, the base
is lattice-complete, and no equalities depend on disregarding cap
boundary mass. The threshold's smaller value at unsampled real bases
is allowed by the theorem and is correctly distinguished from its
integer sampling requirement.

No correction was needed. No numerical computation is a premise of
this audit.
